title: Birds are living dinosaurs
provenance: WP0 worker-curated from general paleontology consensus; NO web access in Phase 4. Every claim needs a source check before WP4 uses this pack for scoring.

claims.claim: Birds are a living branch of theropod dinosaurs, so by modern classification birds are dinosaurs.
claims.source_hint: Gauthier 1986; Brusatte et al., Current Biology 2015 'The Origin and Diversification of Birds'

claims.claim: Only some lineages of birds (the ancestors of today's crown-group birds, Neornithes) survived the end-Cretaceous extinction ~66 Mya; all non-avian dinosaurs and other early bird lineages (e.g. enantiornithines) died out. Source does not say 'beaked'.
Archaeopteryx, from about 150 million years ago, had feathers together with teeth and a long bony tail.
Feathered non-avian dinosaurs such as Sinosauropteryx have been found in Liaoning, China.

The bird wishbone (furcula) is formed by midline fusion of the clavicles; furculae occur in nearly all major theropod clades, including many non-avian theropods. Source does not specifically confirm Tyrannosaurus.
Schweitzer et al. 2005 reported endosteal bone tissue in T. rex marrow cavities and hypothesized it is homologous to avian medullary bone (debated); not established as identical.

honesty_note: Say 'birds ARE dinosaurs', not 'descended from something like dinosaurs'; do not call Tyrannosaurus 'a chicken'.
